receipt_statuses.label: Pending Submission
receipt_statuses.meaning: The filing was created but has not been successfully submitted yet.

receipt_statuses.label: Submitted
receipt_statuses.meaning: The filing was successfully submitted but had not yet been reviewed by the court.

receipt_statuses.label: Filed
receipt_statuses.meaning: All documents and requests in the submission were accepted/filed by the court.

receipt_statuses.label: Partially Filed
receipt_statuses.meaning: Some documents or requests were accepted/filed and some were not filed.

receipt_statuses.label: Not Filed
receipt_statuses.meaning: All documents and requests in the submission were not filed.

jurisdictions.name: Oklahoma — OUCMS district-court civil e-filing
jurisdictions.route_scope: Oklahoma's published e-filing rules and Version 2 civil-filing guide, plus the current registration screen. District-court implementation and permitted case types vary; no current county-by-case-type route was live-tested.
jurisdictions.claim_text: Official materials document a civil e-filing workflow with file attachments and clerk-issued receipt states, but the published rules, current registration screen, and new-case guide give different signals about unrepresented filers and eligible new civil cases. Current access and case-type coverage remain unverified.
jurisdictions.summary: Public materials show a filer-scope mismatch: the indexed rules describe registration and filing by an unrepresented party in a specific case after required registration; the current registration page says pro se filings are not supported; and the Version 2 guide limits its listed new civil-case filings to Oklahoma registered attorneys and state agency representatives. The guide documents PDF/JPEG attachments and a separate submission/acceptance receipt flow. The controlling current route and county/case-type availability were not live-tested. This does not establish the workflow for child-welfare intake or verify the truth, source, or safety of submitted content.

access: The indexed Oklahoma e-filing rules say an unrepresented party may register only for the case or cases in which that person is a party (Rule 2(q)(3), Rule 9(a)(3)); Rule 10(a) conditions e-filing on completing the required registration process.
The current OUCMS registration screen says: “Currently Pro Se filings are not supported.” This is an observed public-page statement, not a test of account registration or submission.

The October 14, 2025 Version 2 guide says Oklahoma registered attorneys and state agency representatives may file the listed new civil-case types; it excludes new Small Claims cases. Its separate existing-case list includes process servers.

The January 28, 2025 FAQ says new-case e-filing would be provided in a future release, but the FAQ itself directs readers to the rules as superseding its information. The later Version 2 guide documents a new-civil-case interface.
document_inputs: The Version 2 guide describes text-based PDF filings, non-text-searchable PDF when conversion is not possible, and non-text JPEG images; it shows file attachments and separate documents associated with the same case.
The Version 2 guide states that confidential documents or documents filed under seal cannot be filed through e-filing in that guide version. Current behavior has not been independently reproduced.

A documented file-upload option establishes that the guide describes file attachments. It does not establish content authenticity, source verification, malware controls, or whether a separate child-welfare intake form accepts evidence files.
receipt: Rule 5 distinguishes successful OUCMS receipt of the complete document and attachments, which triggers a date/time submission receipt, from later clerk acceptance.

Under Rule 5, a clerk-accepted document receives an electronic file stamp and an acceptance receipt; for covered district-court submissions accepted by the clerk, the rule says the submission and acceptance receipts serve as proof of filing.

The Version 2 guide documents Pending Submission, Submitted, Filed, Partially Filed, and Not Filed states. Its new-case flow initially uses a temporary reference; the official case number follows clerk acceptance.

what_was_observed: Reviewed the official Oklahoma Rules for E-Filing in Selected Pilot Courts indexed by OSCN, including Rules 1, 2, 5, 9, 10, and 12.
Inspected the current public OUCMS registration screen, which displays a pro se support notice.
Reviewed the OUCMS Version 2 filer guide dated October 14, 2025, including new-case eligibility, document formats, upload screens, and receipt states.
Reviewed the January 28, 2025 FAQ and its notice that the rules supersede its information.
jurisdictions.what_was_tested: Public-source desk review only. No account creation, login, filing, county-by-case-type submission, child-welfare intake, security-control test, or live OUCMS walkthrough was performed. Synthetic tests of Kapukai's separate receipt-state model are software tests, not OUCMS tests.
what_remains_unknown: Whether later court orders or amendments resolve the difference between the indexed rules, current registration screen, and Version 2 guide.
Which counties and case types currently enable each new-civil-case filing option and what steps a self-represented party can use in a specific case.
The exact child-welfare intake form, its accepted inputs, evidence-handling controls, route, and receipt behavior.
Whether any OUCMS file-security, provenance, or content-verification controls operate in production.
jurisdictions.scope_note: This is a dated source comparison for OUCMS district-court civil e-filing, not a finding about a child-welfare petition, emergency-removal process, criminal-case initiation, or any individual filing. The FAQ predates the Version 2 guide and says the e-filing rules supersede FAQ information. Separately, the indexed rules, current registration screen, and new-case guide present different filer-eligibility signals. Keep that mismatch visible until an authoritative current interpretation and county/case-type scope are confirmed.
